chapter: Tenor players, tours and band boys
title: First recordings with Roy Eldridge and Plucking the Bass
summary: He lists the tunes from his first Roy Eldridge sessions, and Hinton recalls his own Plucking the Bass solo with Cab.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Beautiful. Man, I can't tell you that I can hardly think of anybody you missed in going around here. This list of yours here is just unbelievable; all the records you made, all of the hit records you made, the jazz records, these things you made with Roy Eldridge.
Yeah, those were my first recordings, and I will always remember High Society, Muskrat Ramble, Plucking the Bass, It's My Turn Now, You're a Lucky Guy.
All these were done with Roy, right?

Roy Eldridge, right. Who Told You I Cared? Does Your Heart Beat For Me, I'm Getting Sentimental Over You, Can't Get Started With You -- oh, all these things -- these were my first recordings which I shall always remember. Never forget those.

Well my first recording, I think with Cab Calloway, if I remember correctly, as a soloist was doing Plucking the Bass, which was written by Roy Eldridge and Edgar Battles, and I did it with Cab Calloway.
You're kidding. Oh yes, that's right -- I remember that.
And my first solo in a big name band.
Yeah, I do remember that. Well,

the bass player, Ted Sturgis with Roy Eldridge, he made " Plucking the Base. Yeah. Because we used to play that at the Arcadia, and it used to go over very big. And then, you know, I did all of those things with Lucky Millinder.
